# Level meter (`level-meter`)

Audio level with peak hold, horizontal or vertical.

Group: Charts & instruments. Styles: `import '@mosaic-home/design-system/css/charts';` (or `style.css`).

## Web API

`createLevelMeter` (types in `dist/web/charts/levelMeter.d.ts`): `.mh-level-meter`: audio level per channel with peak hold. The bar shows `--mh-success`, then `--mh-warning` from the warning level and `--mh-danger` from the danger level; the peak marker stays put for a moment, then falls. Horizontal or `--vertical`, smooth or `--segmented`. Built for frame-rate updates: `setLevels` only touches attributes.

```ts
export function createLevelMeter(options: LevelMeterOptions): LevelMeterHandle;

export interface LevelMeterOptions {
  /** Current level per channel in dB (dBFS by default: -60 to 0). `-Infinity` is silence. */
  levels: readonly number[];
  /** The accessible name ("Microphone level"). */
  label: string;
  /** Short channel names shown beside each bar ("L", "R"); also part of each bar's accessible name. */
  channels?: readonly string[];
  /** Bottom and top of the scale in dB (default -60 and 0). */
  min?: number;
  max?: number;
  /** Where the bar turns amber and red (default -12 and -3 dB). */
  warning?: number;
  danger?: number;
  /** Peak markers per channel, in dB. Without them `createLevelMeter` holds the peaks itself. */
  peaks?: readonly number[];
  /** How long a peak stays before it falls, in ms (default 1500), and how fast it falls in dB per second (default 20). */
  peakHold?: number;
  peakDecay?: number;
  orientation?: 'horizontal' | 'vertical';
  /** dB tick labels along the bars. */
  scale?: boolean;
  /** LED-style segments instead of a smooth bar. */
  segmented?: boolean;
  size?: ChartSize;
}

export interface LevelMeterHandle {
  el: HTMLDivElement;
  /** New levels; peaks are held and released over time (`now` in ms, default `performance.now()`). */
  setLevels(levels: readonly number[], now?: number): void;
  update(options: LevelMeterOptions): void;
}
```

## Web example

```ts
import { createLevelMeter } from '@mosaic-home/design-system/web';

const meter = createLevelMeter({
  levels: [-Infinity, -Infinity],
  channels: ['L', 'R'],
  label: 'Speaker output',
  scale: true,
});

// Feed it levels in dBFS, for example from an audio analyser; peaks are held and fall back on their own.
const tick = (now: number): void => {
  const base = -18 + 8 * Math.sin(now / 900);
  meter.setLevels([Math.min(0, base + Math.random() * 8), Math.min(0, base - 3 + Math.random() * 8)], now);
  requestAnimationFrame(tick);
};
requestAnimationFrame(tick);

document.body.append(meter.el);
```

## React API

`LevelMeter` (types in `dist/react/charts.d.ts`): Same DOM and classes as `createLevelMeter`. Without `peaks` it holds the peaks itself from the levels it is rendered with (re-render with new levels, for example once per animation frame).

```ts
export function LevelMeter({ className, ...options }: LevelMeterProps);

export interface LevelMeterProps extends LevelMeterOptions {
  className?: string;
}
```

## React example

```tsx
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { LevelMeter } from '@mosaic-home/design-system/react';

export function LevelMeterExample() {
  const [levels, setLevels] = useState([-Infinity, -Infinity]);
  useEffect(() => {
    // Levels in dBFS, for example from an audio analyser; the meter holds the peaks itself.
    let frame = 0;
    const tick = (now: number) => {
      const base = -18 + 8 * Math.sin(now / 900);
      setLevels([Math.min(0, base + Math.random() * 8), Math.min(0, base - 3 + Math.random() * 8)]);
      frame = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
    };
    frame = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
    return () => cancelAnimationFrame(frame);
  }, []);
  return <LevelMeter levels={levels} channels={['L', 'R']} label="Speaker output" scale />;
}
```
